answer: When several identities cheat in the same epoch, the network treats them as one garden: it traces their correlated failures to a shared operator root, and if the pattern matches, it slashes all their bonds together instead of one at a time. A lone honest agent risks only its own stake at the summit of its record, while a sybil fleet that coordinates fraud loses every bond at once — the beacon is the correlated signal itself. Adding a head therefore multiplies the loss, not the reward, so each extra clone raises the attack's total price.
